subject: Dominant Markers reading as codominant markers??

messages.author: d89993b905b0ab8c
messages.subject: Dominant Markers reading as codominant markers??
parts:
Hi There, 

I formatted my data according to the rootrot.csv file as in example file for AFLP markers (presence=1, absence =0).  When I put missing value as -1, it gives me diploid individuals and if I put NA for missing values it gives me codominant markers; when I read the file using command "mydata <- read.genalex(x$files)" .I could not figure out the reason for this. I have attached a copy of my file format (missing value = na) in this example. 

Also, if I am looking for recombination and migration in the same field for three years and data is collected in three successive years. Is it better to consider them as the same population or different? Is there a way to say in the program that the isolates are from the same field but were collected from different years. 


Thanking you for your help. 

Kind Regards, 
Barsha

messages.subject: Re: Dominant Markers reading as codominant markers??
parts:
Hi everyone, 

I have figured out the way to read the genalex file format in poppr, which read correctly for a haploid and dominant marker. While formatting in genalex file format missing value should be entered as -1. Then, when reading file in R studio, "mydata <- read.genalex(x$files, ploidy = 1, geo = FALSE, region = FALSE, genclone = TRUE, sep = ",", recode = FALSE); where ploidy = 1 stand for haploid organism. 
 
If anyone of you could provide me with an answer to below question, I would be grateful.

"I am looking for recombination and migration in the same field for three years and data is collected in three successive years. Is it better to consider them as the same population or different? Is there a way to say in the program that the isolates are from the same field but were collected from different years."

Hi Barsha,

Thank you for your patience. I was unavailable for the past few days due to the holidays here in the US.

To answer your question, you should use the "strata" feature. As this has been covered in several resources I will point you there:

http://grunwaldlab.github.io/Population_Genetics_in_R/Data_Preparation.html
https://github.com/thibautjombart/adegenet/wiki/Tutorials

Hope that helps,
Zhian
